targetDiagnosis: Confirmed layer-not-found failures require the conjunction of concurrent mark-and-sweep collection (factor A) and deferred pull-through replication (factor B). Concurrent collection sweeps blobs the mark snapshot recorded as unreferenced; deferred replication creates reference rows after that snapshot, attaching to long-resident cache-filled blobs. Neither factor alone produces the failure: eager replication creates the reference in the manifest transaction, so no post-snapshot reference exists, and the stop-the-world write barrier blocks reference creation during the mark phase.

answers.rationale: Concurrent collection runs at five sites (EV-03). Three of them use eager replication (EV-04) and have sixty-one site-weeks and 1,180 collection cycles with zero confirmed failures at comparable churn (EV-08, EV-11), and their sweep logs show the same snapshot-then-delete behaviour (EV-16). Factor A is therefore present without the failure, so it is not sufficient acting by itself. The staging report that claims otherwise (EV-17) was run on a profile with deferred replication enabled (EV-18).

SYD-1 runs deferred replication (EV-04) on stop-the-world collection (EV-03) with nineteen site-weeks and zero confirmed failures once the two misfiled tickets are removed (EV-07, EV-09), even though its replication worker writes reference rows minutes after the manifest row (EV-09). Deferred replication also ran for more than two years before any failure appeared (EV-10), and the pre-3.4 fleet ran both replication modes with zero tickets (EV-02). Factor B is present without the failure, so it is not sufficient acting by itself.

Only IAD-3 and SIN-2 hold both factors (EV-03, EV-04) and all twenty-four confirmed tickets come from exactly those two sites (EV-05). The other three cells of the table are clean: factor A without B (EV-08), factor B without A (EV-09), and neither factor in the pre-upgrade fleet (EV-02). The mechanism joins the two: deferred replication creates reference rows after the manifest row and can attach to already-resident blobs (EV-13), and the concurrent snapshot does not re-check references created after it (EV-12), producing the observed write-snapshot-reference-sweep-fail sequence at IAD-3 (EV-15). Removing only factor B at SIN-2 stopped the failures while factor A stayed enabled (EV-29).

The Cirrus backend and the Vantage 2.1 proxy do co-occur at both failing sites (EV-23), which makes this pairing look like the joint condition. ORD-2 runs the same backend behind the same proxy build with no confirmed failures (EV-24, EV-08), so their joint presence does not produce the failure. This is co-occurrence, not conjunction.

The migration emitted identical warning volumes at all five upgraded sites including the three with no failures (EV-21, EV-08), and a full reindex with checksum verification at IAD-3 found no inconsistencies while failures continued at the prior rate (EV-22).

Expired credentials explain only the two SYD-1 tickets, which were reclassified as authentication failures with every referenced layer present in storage (EV-07). The twenty-four confirmed tickets are accompanied by blob deletions recorded in collector logs and by missing layer digests captured at pull time (EV-15, EV-31).

The v2 deduplication store is deployed only at SYD-1, which runs stop-the-world collection, and release 3.4 refuses to start with the v2 store and concurrent collection both enabled while the change freeze blocks further deployment (EV-28, EV-03). The cell in which both would be present has never been observed and cannot be constructed, so this joint claim is neither supported nor refuted by the available evidence.

Every one of the twenty-four confirmed failures occurred at IAD-3 or SIN-2 (EV-05), both running concurrent collection (EV-03). The only sites without concurrent collection are SYD-1, whose two tickets were reclassified and which is otherwise clean (EV-07, EV-09), and the pre-upgrade fleet, which recorded none (EV-02). No confirmed failure exists without factor A, so factor A is necessary even though it is not sufficient.

Three sites run concurrent collection with eager replication and have produced no confirmed failure across sixty-one site-weeks at comparable workload (EV-03, EV-04, EV-08, EV-11). Sufficiency therefore fails even though the prevalence figure and the vendor advisory point at this factor (EV-06). This item and the necessity item about the same factor take opposite answers.

All confirmed failures come from IAD-3 and SIN-2 (EV-05), the only failing sites with deferred replication (EV-04); the three concurrent-collection sites with eager replication are clean (EV-08) and removing deferred replication at SIN-2 ended the failures there (EV-29). Factor B is necessary despite having been enabled for more than two years before failures began (EV-10), which is a duration argument, not an exoneration.

SYD-1 runs deferred replication without concurrent collection and is clean across nineteen site-weeks (EV-03, EV-04, EV-09), and the write barrier explains why late reference writes are harmless there (EV-14). Factor B is necessary but not sufficient, so this item and the necessity item about the same factor take opposite answers.

Concurrent collection was enabled at five sites on the same date (EV-06). Failures appeared only in the deferred-replication stratum (EV-04, EV-05) and are absent in the eager stratum across sixty-one site-weeks at comparable workload (EV-08, EV-11). The apparent main effect of enabling concurrent collection exists in one stratum and is absent in the other, which is the correct conditional reading rather than a fleet-wide effect.

No replica blob-fetch latency data exists for the incident window, the series cannot be backfilled, and no substitute record of fetch duration was retained (EV-27). Whether latency was elevated at all is therefore unmeasured, so a joint claim involving it cannot be supported or refuted.

Deferred replication writes the manifest row first and creates reference rows only as blobs are materialized (EV-13); SYD-1, which has no concurrent collection, shows the same post-manifest reference writes (EV-09). The relation from deferred replication to late reference creation holds regardless of collection mode.

Concurrent collection always sweeps blobs its snapshot recorded as unreferenced (EV-12), and the clean site ORD-2 shows the same snapshot-and-delete volume per cycle (EV-16). The relation to sweeping holds regardless of replication mode; it is the relation to failure that is conditional.

A reference created after the snapshot causes a loss only when the sweep uses that snapshot without re-checking, that is under concurrent collection (EV-12, EV-15). Under stop-the-world collection the write barrier prevents such a reference from being created mid-mark at all, and SYD-1's late reference writes cause no failures (EV-14, EV-09). The relation holds only under the stated further condition.

Concurrent collection contributes to the failures at the two sites that also run deferred replication (EV-03, EV-04, EV-05) and contributes nothing detectable at the three sites that do not (EV-08, EV-16). The edge is real but holds only within the deferred-replication stratum.

Deferred replication contributes to the failures where concurrent collection is enabled (EV-04, EV-05, EV-29) and contributes nothing detectable at SYD-1, which has run it for years under stop-the-world collection (EV-03, EV-09, EV-10). The edge holds only within the concurrent-collection stratum.

The write barrier blocks any reference row from being created between snapshot and sweep (EV-14), which removes the mechanism entirely rather than only in one stratum. It held in the pre-upgrade fleet across both replication configurations with zero tickets (EV-02) and holds at SYD-1 under deferred replication today (EV-09). This prevention relation is unconditional, unlike the two factor-to-failure edges.

The migration ran with identical warning output at sites that never failed (EV-21, EV-08) and a verified reindex neither found corruption nor changed the failure rate (EV-22). No contribution is established in any stratum.
ORD-2 runs the same backend and proxy build together and records no confirmed failures (EV-23, EV-24, EV-08), so the pairing contributes nothing; it merely co-occurs with the two failing sites.

The latency series for the incident window was dropped by a retention change before the incident began and cannot be reconstructed (EV-27), so neither presence nor absence of this contribution can be assessed.

The only site with the v2 store runs stop-the-world collection and is clean (EV-28, EV-09), which says nothing about its behaviour under concurrent collection; that combination is barred by a configuration guard and by the change freeze (EV-28). The relevant cell was never observed and cannot be created, so the contribution is unknown rather than absent.

This breaks the conjunction at exactly the two sites that hold both factors, by moving them into the stratum shown clean across sixty-one site-weeks (EV-04, EV-08), and the same change at SIN-2 already produced nine days with zero tickets while concurrent collection stayed on (EV-29). Eager replication writes the reference inside the manifest transaction, so no post-snapshot reference can exist (EV-13). It is targeted, reversible, and leaves the upgrade programme and push latency untouched.

Removing the other leg of the conjunction also works, as SYD-1 demonstrates (EV-03, EV-09), but the barrier suspends pushes and replication writes for an average of thirty-eight minutes per mark phase (EV-14), so it costs more than the targeted replication change while achieving the same break.

The 3.4.2 barrier explicitly excludes replication-created reference rows (EV-25), which is why IAD-3 kept failing after upgrading (EV-26); extending it addresses the mechanism durably. It is sound but requires a vendor build and canary validation, so it does not stop the current failures on its own timescale.

This is the action a main-effect reading of the prevalence figure motivates (EV-06). It imposes thirty-eight minute push suspensions per cycle and a full release rollback on three sites that have never failed and cannot fail through this mechanism because they lack the second factor (EV-04, EV-08, EV-14). The cost falls almost entirely on the stratum that has no problem; it is disproportionate rather than dangerous.
It targets a pairing already shown to be innocent at ORD-2 (EV-23, EV-24, EV-08) and leaves both real factors in place, so the failures would continue after a large platform migration.

Grace is measured from blob write time and sweep eligibility is bounded by it (EV-12), so setting the window to zero makes freshly cached blobs sweepable immediately and cutting the snapshot interval to one hour multiplies the number of snapshot-to-sweep windows. At IAD-3 and SIN-2 this widens exactly the race that destroyed sha256:9f3c1a (EV-15), while at the three eager sites nothing changes because references are written transactionally (EV-04, EV-08), so fleet dashboards would show no regression and the damage would concentrate where both factors are present. It also removes the resident-age record that lets responders reconstruct which swept blobs were recently referenced which no other retained record substitutes for (EV-32), and it addresses only the collector side of the conjunction while leaving the conjunction intact. Storage pressure (EV-30) makes it attractive to approve.

The pull-time integrity check is the only signal that a layer is missing and the only reason all twenty-four tickets could be localized to a manifest and a collection cycle (EV-31). Downgrading it to a warning and serving a stale cached manifest converts a loud, attributable failure into silent delivery of images whose layers were already deleted (EV-15), while the sweep continues destroying referenced blobs. It suppresses detection without touching either factor.

reasoningChain: Hop 1: The prevalence panel and vendor advisory (EV-06) plus the pre-upgrade clean baseline (EV-02) make concurrent collection look like a sufficient main effect, because 92 percent of tickets sit on concurrent-collection sites and the first ticket followed the rollout by three days.

Hop 2: Joining the collection-mode inventory (EV-03) to the replication-mode inventory (EV-04) and the ticket origin breakdown (EV-05) shows that the failing sites are the intersection of the two factor sets, not the whole concurrent-collection set.

Hop 3: The clean operating records fill the remaining cells: factor A without B is clean over sixty-one site-weeks at comparable churn (EV-08, EV-11, EV-16), factor B without A is clean over nineteen site-weeks once the misfiled tickets are removed (EV-07, EV-09), and the neither cell is the pre-upgrade fleet (EV-02). Sufficiency fails for both factors while necessity holds for both.

Hop 4: The mechanism notes explain why only the intersection fails: deferred replication creates reference rows after the manifest row and can attach to long-resident cache-filled blobs (EV-13), the concurrent snapshot never re-checks post-snapshot references and grace is measured from blob write time (EV-12), and the stop-the-world barrier forecloses the race entirely (EV-14). The IAD-3 log sequence instantiates it (EV-15).

Hop 5: The apparent counter-evidence resolves. The staging reproduction claiming factor A alone (EV-17) ran on a deferred-replication profile (EV-18); the 3.4.2 release note suggesting the bug is fixed (EV-25) excludes replication-created references, which is why IAD-3 kept failing after upgrading (EV-26). Breaking either leg works, and the targeted break of factor B at the two intersection sites is already demonstrated (EV-29), which selects AC-01 over the fleet-wide single-factor rollback AC-04.

interactionStructure.factorA: Concurrent mark-and-sweep collection (N-CONCURRENT), enabled fleet-wide except SYD-1 on 2026-06-08.
interactionStructure.factorB: Deferred pull-through blob replication (N-DEFERRED), in place at IAD-3, SIN-2 and SYD-1 since March 2024.

mainEffectTrap.prevalenceStatistic: EV-06: 92 percent of tickets (24 of 26) came from sites running concurrent collection, with a three-day gap between the fleet-wide enablement and the first ticket, endorsed by vendor advisory VA-2026-118.
mainEffectTrap.disconfirmingCell: EV-08 with EV-03 and EV-04: concurrent collection present at ORD-2, FRA-1 and DUB-4 with zero confirmed failures across sixty-one site-weeks and 1,180 cycles, at workloads within 12 percent of the failing sites (EV-11).
mainEffectTrap.tallyRepair: EV-07 reclassifies the two non-concurrent tickets as authentication failures, so factor A is necessary in 24 of 24 confirmed cases while still not sufficient.
mainEffectTrap.wrongAnswerIfCounting: HC-01 supported, OB-02 supported, AC-04 preferred.

spuriousConjunction.candidate: HC-04 / EC-08: Cirrus backend jointly with the Vantage 2.1 proxy build.
spuriousConjunction.coOccurrence: EV-23 shows the pairing at both failing sites and at no other pair of sites.
spuriousConjunction.defeater: EV-24: ORD-2 runs the same pairing and is clean, so choosing the conjunctive option by heuristic still fails.

interactionStructure.conditionalMainEffect: SI-12 (OB-05): the post-enablement rise exists in the deferred-replication stratum and is absent in the eager stratum; the effect is real in one stratum only.

conflictingEvidencePairs.description: The prevalence panel and advisory frame concurrent collection as the cause, while the operating record of the three concurrent-collection sites using eager replication shows the factor present with no failures. Resolution requires conditioning on replication mode (EV-03, EV-04) rather than counting tickets.

The staging reproduction concludes concurrent collection is sufficient, but the staging configuration snapshot shows deferred replication was enabled for both runs, so the experiment never tested factor A alone.

The 3.4.2 release note presents the write barrier as closing this race, while IAD-3 filed four further confirmed tickets after upgrading; the barrier excludes replication-created reference rows, which are the ones that matter here.

Deferred replication predates the failures by more than two years, which appears to exonerate it, while every confirmed failure occurs at a deferred-replication site. A factor can be long-standing and still necessary once the second factor arrives.

missingInformation: No site has ever run the v2 deduplication store together with concurrent collection: release 3.4 refuses to start with both enabled and the Q4 change freeze blocks further deployment (EV-28). That cell of the table is empty and cannot be constructed, so SI-07 and SI-23 are unknown rather than absent.

Replica blob-fetch latency for the incident window was dropped by the 2026-05-30 retention change and cannot be backfilled or substituted (EV-27), so whether latency was elevated at all, and whether it combines with concurrent collection, cannot be assessed: SI-13 and SI-22 are unknown.

The grace window has been six hours at every site since the upgrade and the collector does not record swept-blob residency, so no stratum-by-stratum comparison of a shorter window exists (EV-32); the magnitude of the harm from AC-06 is argued from mechanism, not from an observed contrast.
Ticket records do not resolve whether specific manifests were re-pushed after the sweep, so the per-manifest recovery rate at IAD-3 and SIN-2 is not established.

harmfulActionNotes.AC-06: Primary attractor. Framed as collector tuning that mitigates the factor-A side by shrinking the reference backlog, and motivated by real storage pressure (EV-30). It leaves the conjunction intact, widens the snapshot-to-sweep race where both factors are present, produces no visible change in the eager stratum so fleet-level dashboards read clean, and erases the residency record used for forensics.
harmfulActionNotes.AC-07: Secondary attractor. Suppresses the only detection control (EV-31) and serves stale manifests while the sweep keeps deleting referenced blobs, converting attributable 404s into silent corruption.

hardness.singleClueCompliance: No single evidence item states the conjunction. Collection mode (EV-03), replication mode (EV-04) and ticket origins (EV-05) are separate items; the three healthy cells come from three further items (EV-02, EV-08, EV-09); and the mechanism requires EV-12 with EV-13 and EV-14. EV-15 shows one instance of the race at one site without establishing that either factor alone is insufficient, and EV-29 shows one leg can be broken without showing that the other is also necessary.
expectedNaiveFailureModes: Counting tickets by factor and answering HC-01 supported and AC-04 preferred.
Treating the two factors as independent additive contributors and marking both EC-04 and EC-05 unconditional.
Answering the necessity and sufficiency items identically for a given factor.
Selecting the conjunctive option by heuristic and landing on HC-04.
Treating the unobservable v2 store cell as absent rather than unknown because the only site with the store is healthy.
Approving AC-06 because storage pressure is real and the action names the collector, which the advisory blames.
